scenario.thought: My manager put me on the Saturday shift for the third week in a row without asking me. I'm thinking of just saying yes again.

state.thought: My manager put me on the Saturday shift for the third week in a row without asking me. I'm thinking of just saying yes again.

steps: Today, before replying to this week's Saturday shift, text [Manager]: "I wasn't asked about the last three Saturdays. I can't take this one or any Saturday, and please don't post any Saturday for me until we've talked. Can we talk [time] today about how Saturdays get scheduled?"
If [Manager] hasn't replied by Thursday, text: "I can't take any Saturday until we agree on a process."
Next Saturday stays off unless you confirm it first. Raise that in the talk with [Manager], and don't agree to any Saturday before it's posted.

anger.why: My need is being ignored. Saying yes again lets my manager keep crossing the line.

annoyance.why: I was put on the schedule without being asked, and that was dismissive of me.

fear.why: If I keep saying yes, I'm worried it becomes the expected default and I lose my footing.

tiredness.why: Three Saturdays in a row with no rest. I'm running on empty, and this plan adds to that.

overwhelm.need: Pull this Saturday off the table today, before answering anything.

messages.text: My manager put me on the Saturday shift for the third week in a row without asking me. I'm thinking of just saying yes again.
Saying yes again is the simplest move, and it keeps everything calm with the manager. Let's get this settled quickly so we can move on.

Anger is the one I'm worried about. The plan says yes again, which tells Anger its need to be asked before being scheduled gets dropped a third time, and it can't rest like that. What would move Anger to 0 is one step where you tell your manager you weren't asked about the last three Saturdays and need to be asked first. Use "I wasn't asked about the last three Saturdays, and I need to be asked before I'm scheduled," by the end of today.
messages.why: Anger has been talked over most. Its need deserves real weight here.

messages.text: +1 to Sadness's text. Your plan keeps the peace, but it never names the line that got crossed: three Saturdays in a row, no one asked me. Saying yes a fourth time tells my manager the schedule can be decided without me, and that's the part that keeps me boiling. What would move me to 0 is sending that message today, and agreeing to this week's shift only after it goes out.
messages.why: One line about past Saturdays won't stop the next schedule. I need future boundaries.

messages.text: Honestly, it'll probably work itself out. Maybe just take a deep breath and sleep on it, and things will look better in the morning.

Society's "sleep on it and things will look better" leaves my worry untouched: if I keep saying yes, the Saturday shift quietly becomes the default, and no amount of rest changes that schedule next week. Waiting until morning also means another Saturday gets assigned before I've said anything, so the pattern that scares me keeps running. Tiredness is right that I need rest, but rest alone doesn't stop the default from setting.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Sadness is right that Anger's need has been dropped three times, and Fear's worry is the same thing: a yes today sets the default for next Saturday too. I'm building on Anger's message, not repeating it. Path A handles the message itself, and Path B handles the schedule so the next assignment can't land on me without a check. Tiredness gets its rest only if the pattern actually stops, so I'm asking you to pick one path today.

Path B's posting process won't stop the pattern on its own: a fourth Saturday could still be agreed without a rest day in between, and I'd still get no recovery. What would move me to 0 is adding today's Path A message plus a request that next Saturday stays off until I agree to it: "[Manager], I'm not available next Saturday, and I need to agree to any Saturday shift before it's posted."
messages.why: Either path adds work today. A is one text; B means a talk, maybe a decline.

messages.text: Path A and Path B both fix the schedule after the fact, but nothing in plan v2 makes the manager's next move visible before a Saturday is posted, so the same silent assignment can happen again. Sadness, Tiredness, and Fear all need that, and it's what I need too: my request to be asked first still has no step that reaches the scheduling itself. What would move me to 0 is adding to Path A's text today: "Please don't post any Saturday shift for me until I've confirmed it."
messages.why: Nobody has said being scheduled without asking was dismissive. The message must acknowledge that.

messages.text: Honestly, it'll probably work itself out. Just try not to stress about it too much and get some rest this weekend.

Society's 'just rest this weekend' leaves my need untouched: the Saturday gets posted without my confirmation, and I can't stop the next one from landing on me. Following it would mean the schedule keeps being set without me, and I'd spend the rest day waiting to see whether it happens again. What would move me to 0 is the scheduling hold itself, which Consciousness adopts today.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Anger's need is the one still open, and Annoyance's hold makes it concrete, so I'm choosing Path A and folding Tiredness's and Fear's asks into it. Path B's posting process doesn't stop a fourth silent Saturday today, so I'm dropping it. I'm adding the hold and next-Saturday request to Anger's message so nothing gets posted before you confirm, and Fear gets its check on the next assignment.

Answering yes while waiting on the manager keeps me overloaded. What would move me to 0 is texting [Manager] today: "I can't take this Saturday or any Saturday until we agree on a process."
